dialect.detail: Likely GnuCOBOL or similar open-source/PC COBOL targeting file-based batch processing; SOURCE-COMPUTER/OBJECT-COMPUTER set to IBM-370 but uses ACCEPT FROM COMMAND-LINE, LINE SEQUENTIAL files, and a debug comment referencing 'debug\cobolexec.ctl' (Windows path), suggesting GnuCOBOL on Windows or similar PC environment

purpose.domain_detail: CUNA (Credit Union National Association?) mail/document processing utility; reads input records and filters/counts by mail type categories (PRESORTS, RESIDUALS, NO MAILS, HANDSTUFFS, PDF)
purpose.summary: A batch utility program that reads an input file, processes records looking for a '%FILENAME%' marker, writes matching records to an output file, and counts records by mail processing category (presorts, residuals, no mails, handstuffs, PDF). It reads configuration from a control file passed via command-line argument and logs results to a syslog file.

notable_features: ACCEPT FROM COMMAND-LINE for runtime configuration
Control file parsing with UNSTRING DELIMITED BY
Multiple file status checks with STRING error messages
Tab character visible in PROCEDURE DIVISION (mixed indentation)
verdict.notes: The file has mixed line numbering styles (some lines have 6-digit sequence numbers like 000022, others have no sequence numbers), suggesting the code was edited in a non-mainframe editor. A tab character appears in the 200-PROCESS paragraph. The PROGRAM-ID paragraph appears to be missing from the IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. The COPY FORMCP copybook is referenced but not shown, so some working-storage fields (WS-MCP-* variables, WS-CONTROL-FILE-*, WS-SYSLOG-*, EOF-CTL, WS-EOF-CTL) are defined there. IP-FILE1-STATUS is declared in working-storage but appears unused (file status uses WS-MCP-SYSIN1-STATUS from copybook).
